subclasses.name: Soulknife
subclasses.d: Use psychic powers to create psychic blades that need no equipment, bypass many resistances, and deal psychic damage. Psi-Bolstered Knack helps with skill checks.

subclasses.name: Arcane Trickster
subclasses.d: Add wizard spellcasting and excel at using Mage Hand in unique ways. Build around True Strike and Intelligence for an Int-based attack Rogue.

subclasses.name: Assassin
subclasses.d: Masters of infiltration and deadly surprise. Devastating Sneak Attacks at the start of combat. Excels when campaigns support preparation time.

subclasses.name: Thief
subclasses.d: Move quickly, act quickly, and use magic items better than anyone else. Fast Hands unlocks the Healer feat trick — probably the best use of that feat in the game.

species.d: Two extra skills, perpetual Advantage on Charisma checks, and built-in disguises. Excellent for a Face build.
Tailor-made for the Rogue. Brave covers your weakest defense. Halfling Nimbleness lets you move through enemies' spaces. Naturally Stealthy lets you hide behind allies.
An additional skill and an Origin Feat on top of your Background's feat. Easy choice on any build.
Spider Climb and a Bite attack for a bonus Sneak Attack option. Good for a melee Rogue who wants a vampire aesthetic.
Darkvision, Keen Senses (Perception), and immunity to sleep effects. Wood Elves get extra speed and can hide in light obscurement.
Gnomish Cunning grants Advantage on Int/Wis/Cha saves vs. magic — extremely useful. Forest Gnomes add minor illusions.
Extra skill proficiency and a bonus to Charisma checks. Solid if you want to play a half-elf Face Rogue.
+1 to AC, no need to eat or breathe, immunity to disease. Durable in a way most Rogues aren't.
Healing Hands and Darkvision are nice, but the damage forms (Radiant Soul etc.) don't complement a Sneak Attack playstyle well.
Breath Weapon and elemental resistances are fine features, but nothing here is specifically useful to the Rogue.
Dwarven Resilience (poison resistance and advantage on saves) is genuinely good, but speed reduction hurts a mobile Rogue.
Giant's Power adds Str-based options that you won't use, and Stone's Endurance competes with your Bonus Action. Situational.
Psychic resistance is useful, but the rest is very campaign-dependent. Good if the DM uses a lot of mind-affecting magic.
Shapeshifting is flavorful, but this version lacks the mechanical bite of the EFotA Changeling. Situational.
Adrenaline Rush gives extra mobility on a Bonus Action, which competes with Cunning Action. Relentless Endurance is solid insurance.
Cold-flavored abilities rarely align with a Rogue's core tactics. The slow effect can be useful situationally.
Shifting provides a burst of survivability, but you'd rather use your bonus action. Best for melee builds who need a panic button.
Hellish Rebuke is a nice reaction and Darkvision is always welcome, but Infernal Legacy doesn't directly improve Rogue tactics.

abilityNotes.n: Dump stat. Nothing a typical Rogue does uses Strength.
Your primary ability. Skills, tools, attacks, damage, AC, and your best save. Your Background must increase this.
Hit points are always important, especially for melee Rogues who draw more attacks.
Arcane Tricksters need it for spells. Others only need it for Investigation.
Helpful for Insight, Perception, and saves. Slippery Mind (level 15) adds Wisdom save proficiency.
Rogues make a great Face. You can't be effective without Charisma if you plan to fill that role.

skills.d: Functionally useless. Sleight of Hand handles manacles and rope better.
Very helpful, but not as important as Perception.
Most important skill in the game. Several party members should have it even if you're great at it.
Essential for a Face. Expertise here is devastating.
Now used to pick locks. Proficient in both Sleight of Hand and Thieves' Tools: use the higher modifier and roll with Advantage.
A Rogue without Stealth is a very strange Rogue.

backgrounds.d: Good ability scores, great feat, fantastic skills if you're playing Face. (ABoH)
Absolutely fantastic for the Rogue — especially in a small party or for a Face build. (PHB)
Perfect for a stealthy character. (PHB)
Excellent ability scores and skills. Great access to Booming Blade or True Strike for non-AT builds. (FRHoF)
Easy go-to, especially in a small party needing skill coverage. Good stats, good skills, Skilled gives even more. (PHB)
Good ability scores, good skills, and Lucky. Tool proficiency is redundant but everything else is excellent. (PHB)
Good skill coverage. Basically Scribe but with different fixed skills. Good for small parties. (EFotA)
Great ability scores, decent skills. Magic Initiate (Druid) can give useful utility options. (PHB)
Works for an Int-based Arcane Trickster. Alert offsets lower Dexterity for initiative. (EFotA)
Good ability scores for any Rogue with decent Intelligence. (FRHoF)
Good ability scores and skills for a Cha-investing Rogue. Zhentarim Ruffian is excellent. (FRHoF)
Could build around True Strike for Int-based attacks, but you'll likely get more value from Human + Magic Initiate. (PHB)
Good ability scores for an Arcane Trickster, decent skills, but Crafter is not a great feat. (PHB)
Good ability scores and Musician is welcome in any party, but the skills are nearly useless for a Rogue. (PHB)
Could work for an Int-based Arcane Trickster, but Scribe has better skills. (PHB)
Int and Con work for Arcane Trickster, but you're still a Rogue first — you really need Dexterity. (PHB)
Decent ability scores, one good skill, but Tavern Brawler is useless on a Rogue. (PHB)
Good ability scores, but Savage Attacker is wasted on the Rogue and the skills aren't great. (PHB)
Bad ability scores, bad feat, bad skills. (FRHoF)
Bad ability scores, bad skills. (PHB)
Bad ability scores. If you want Alert, look at Inquisitive. (PHB)
Not good enough to justify the lack of a Dexterity increase. (PHB)

feats.d: The Thief Rogue's Fast Hands lets you use Battle Medic as a Bonus Action — probably the best use of Healer in the entire game.
An easy choice on any character. Three extra d20 rolls per long rest on attacks, checks, or saves.
Proficiency in Insight or Persuasion, and give Heroic Inspiration to your whole party once per day. Excellent if you don't need something else. (FRHoF)
Heroic Inspiration is always useful. A great choice on literally any character. (ABoH)
Opportunity Attacks can effectively double your damage output. Gives your whole party Advantage on initiative. (FRHoF)
Never a bad choice, but less impactful for Assassins who already get Advantage on initiative.
Standard builds can use buffs like Guidance or Mage Armor. Arcane Tricksters can build around True Strike for Int-based attacks.
A great way to contribute to any party.
Rogues get more skills than anyone else, but a small party may still need more coverage.
Timely Retreat is really good. (ABoH)
Faerie Fire may help Arcane Tricksters, but you already have easy Advantage from Cunning Action. (LFL)
Neat but not especially impactful. Crafting mundane gear stops mattering early and omits the Herbalist Kit.
1d6 damage isn't worth Concentration, but Hex's debuff on Wisdom ability checks helps you stay hidden. (LFL)
The Help Action isn't useful enough to justify this unless you're a Hobgoblin. (FRHoF)
Your weapon damage die isn't a big enough part of your output to make this impactful.
Rogues lean too heavily on Bonus Action to make this an easy choice. (FRHoF)
You should literally never make an unarmed strike.
If you need this, you need to be using Cunning Action more to stay safely out of reach.
Grab a weapon with Nick and you roll at least two d20s per turn, dramatically improving Sneak Attack reliability.
This feat was made for the Rogue. Absolutely essential if you plan to fight at range — missing doesn't reveal you.
A climb speed is the next best thing to flight. Standing up quickly from prone and reduced jump run-up both help in combat.
Helpful for Arcane Tricksters. Misty Step may be redundant with Cunning Action, but more spells and free castings add real utility.
A massive amount of temporary hit points. Wait until you have 20 Dexterity first since it can't improve Dex.
Nearly all your preferred weapons deal Piercing. The reroll can target any damage die — including Sneak Attack dice.
Never a bad choice. Hard to pick the right ability until you have 20 Dex and all the feats you want.
Potentially an easy way to get Sneak Attack outside your own turn via Opportunity Attacks.
You're almost certainly going to learn Invisibility. Free castings are a reliable bonus.
Helpful for ranged builds but not essential.
More skills are always nice, especially once you have Reliable Talent at level 7.
Too situational on its own, though it nicely complements Assassin infiltration.
Combine Cunning Action (Dash) with the push to rush into melee, knock target back, then retreat. Niche but functional.
Won't contribute meaningfully to Rogue capabilities, but THP snacks are always welcome.
Too much overlap with Uncanny Dodge.
Even for the Arcane Trickster, this is hard to justify.
Great insurance against mental saves, but hiding keeps you untargetable. High-level Slippery Mind reduces the appeal further.
Competes too much with crucial class features and action economy.
Poisoning before combat is less of a hassle for Rogues than multi-attack classes. Damage doesn't scale with level.
Rogues get very few slashing Sneak Attack weapons, but this can work with whips.
Too situational.
Too situational.
Potentially useful for Arcane Tricksters, but not strictly necessary.
Not worth the feat. Use Steady Aim for Advantage while still rolling two d20s to hit.
Rogues' Sneak Attack weapons almost all deal Piercing. Crusher needs bludgeoning and doesn't give a Dexterity increase.
Bad and conflicts with your crucial Bonus Action class features.
Rogues should not be grappling.
The ability score increase is useless and you'll only get the damage bonus once per round.
Ruins stealth.
A 1-level Fighter dip is almost always a better idea unless you expect to reach level 20.
Borderline worthless. Put +2 into Dexterity and wear light armor.
You should not be using a polearm to attack.
Not even on an Arcane Trickster.
You don't get proficiency with shields.
You have Cunning Action.
You cannot use Sneak Attack with spell attacks.
You already get enough Weapon Mastery slots from your class.
Grants cantrips and a leveled spell (recharges on long rest). The d8 chaos die is a risk, but the free spellcasting is genuinely useful for a Rogue who wants utility without a multiclass dip.

Arcane Eye and See Invisibility are excellent, but your spell save DC is Int-based — not a natural fit unless you're an Arcane Trickster. The skill bonuses help an investigation-focused build. (Eberron)
Hunter's Mark and terrain-based advantage are more Ranger-flavored than Rogue. The perception bonus is nice, but this is a heavy investment for situational gains. (Eberron)
Animal-focused abilities rarely see use in a typical dungeon campaign. Almost nothing here benefits the Rogue's core tactics. (Eberron)
Cure Wounds spells and a bonus to Medicine checks fit a supportive Rogue in a small party. Pairs well with the Thief's Fast Hands to use Healer as a Bonus Action. (Eberron)
Friends and Unseen Servant are flavorful but rarely impactful in combat. Good for roleplay-heavy or social campaigns. (Eberron)
Fabricate and Identify are highly useful utility spells. The bonus to tool checks improves your Thieves' Tools rolls. Good pick for a Rogue who wants out-of-combat utility. (Eberron)
Misty Step and enhanced movement align perfectly with the mobile Rogue's playstyle. Extra escape options for when Cunning Action isn't enough. (Eberron)
Sending and Comprehend Languages are useful utility but niche in combat. Best in political or intrigue campaigns where communication matters. (Eberron)
Alert and Guardian of Faith lean more Fighter/Paladin. The initiative bonus is nice, but most of the spell list doesn't fit the Rogue's action economy. (Eberron)
Invisibility and Darkness are excellent for a stealthy Rogue who wants more sneaking options beyond Cunning Action. Pairs especially well with Skulker. (Eberron)
Gust of Wind and Fog Cloud can help with escape or positioning, but most Rogues already have plenty of mobility. Situational. (Eberron)
Alarm and Arcane Lock are useful utility for dungeon security and infiltration prep, but contribute little in direct combat. (Eberron)

epicBoons.d: Functionally removes your ability to miss. If you used two-weapon fighting for a second Sneak Attack chance, you can safely stop.
Stunningly powerful combined with Reliable Talent. Every proficient skill becomes extraordinary.
Great on a melee build where you draw many attacks.
Immunity to poison is great, and Cunning Strike lets you trade 1d6 damage for 2d6 poison which you can then reroll. (FRHoF)
Extra movement is nice, but you can already Disengage as a Bonus Action.
Excellent for a stealthy Rogue. Note that Hide, Search, and Study are Actions that break the invisibility.
Probably your only built-in option for handling invisible enemies at high levels.
More useful to support allies' save-or-suck spells than for anything you're doing.
You don't attack frequently enough for the damage boost to be meaningful. Magic weapon handles resistance.
Last Stand is great insurance, but not enough to justify as your first Epic Boon.

classFeatures.d: Doubles proficiency on two chosen skills at level 1, two more at level 6. Rogues get Expertise earlier than any other class.
Central combat mechanic. Once per turn (not per round) — can trigger on reactions too. A 65% hit chance means missing 1-in-3; get Advantage.
Rarely impactful in play. 2024 update: also grants an extra language proficiency.
New in 2024. Rogues get 2 slots. Vex grants Advantage (qualifies for Sneak Attack); Nick enables a bonus attack for a second d20 roll.
Central to all Rogue tactics. Ranged builds Hide between attacks; melee builds Dash or Disengage to strike and retreat safely.
Good backup when other Sneak Attack tactics fail, but prevents movement — leaving you very exposed.
Massive expansion of combat options. Trade Sneak Attack dice for rider effects: Poison (Con save), Trip (prone), or Withdraw (free movement).
Halve damage from one attack per round as a reaction. Huge damage mitigation over the course of a combat.
Two more Expertise choices. You now have four skills at double proficiency.
Between Evasion and Uncanny Dodge you are very durable. Half or no damage on Dex-save effects.
Minimum roll of 10 on any proficient skill check. Especially powerful for Expertise skills. Moved from level 11 in 2024.
Use up to two Cunning Strike effects on the same attack. Combining two Con-save effects gives decent odds at least one sticks.
More Cunning Strike options. Costlier but more impactful: Daze, Knock Out, Obscure.
Proficiency in both Wisdom and Charisma saves. With Dex and Int already covered, you now have broad save protection.
Not always relevant, but excellent protection when you'd otherwise be very vulnerable.
Works on any d20 test — turn a miss into a hit or a failed check into a 20. At least one guaranteed critical hit per rest.

optional.d: Poisoned is a massive debuff, but targets Constitution saves (consistently high). Resistance and immunity to poison are also common.
Knocking an enemy prone benefits your whole party. Especially useful against flying enemies — prone causes most to fall.
Somewhat redundant with Cunning Action but very useful for melee builds. Combine with Cunning Action Dash for extreme retreat range.
Gamble less Sneak Attack damage than Knock Out but still extremely impactful. Works on targets immune to unconsciousness.
A huge gamble — 6d6 Sneak Attack dice to apply Unconscious. Targets Constitution saves (high). Needs Bane or Mind Sliver support to be reliable.
Most creatures have mediocre Dexterity. Blinded is a significant debuff that will be reliably impactful for your whole career.

weapons.d: The cornerstone of two-weapon fighting. Nick mastery gives a free bonus attack so you roll two d20s per turn, dramatically improving Sneak Attack reliability. Take Piercer to reroll any damage die — including Sneak Attack dice.
Pair with a dagger. Vex grants Advantage on your next attack after a hit, qualifying for Sneak Attack without spending Cunning Action.
Your best long-range option. If hiding and sniping with Cunning Action is your plan, this is your weapon. Slow mastery can lock down fast enemies.
The go-to secondary weapon for two-weapon fighting — largest damage die of any weapon with Nick. Use a dagger instead if you're taking Piercer.
Larger damage die than the shortsword, but a dagger secondary gives you a second d20 roll that easily makes up the difference in average damage.
Perfectly fine, but if you can make sniping work the light crossbow is clearly better for the Slow mastery and the extra range.
Little reason to use for two-weapon fighting — you could use a hand crossbow and a dagger without eating your Bonus Action. Cunning Action is non-negotiable.

armor.d: You're going to live in this. Maximizing Dexterity makes it competitive with medium or heavy armor — with no stealth penalty.

multiclass.d: Ritual casting plus Booming Blade, True Strike, and Find Familiar. Have your familiar use Help for guaranteed Advantage (and Sneak Attack) on every attack.

Booming Blade cantrip plus powerful Infusions (Enhanced Defense, Goggles of Night). Three levels unlocks Armorer's Infiltrator Armor: Advantage on Stealth and a Dex-based ranged attack that qualifies for Sneak Attack.
Two more Expertise choices and a splash of spellcasting. Clean, low-investment dip.
Archery Fighting Style is a significant improvement for ranged builds. Two-Weapon Fighting is a trap — the +2–3 damage bonus is irrelevant next to Sneak Attack scaling.
One level for a Fighting Style and Hunter's Mark. Three levels for Gloom Stalker, which makes many dungeon and wilderness campaigns dramatically easier.

Bonus Action attacks can't apply Sneak Attack. Unarmored Defense (Wis-based) won't beat studded leather with high Dexterity. Way of Shadow at 3 levels is decent but a large investment for something you're already built for.
Reckless Attack only works with Strength-based attacks — never good for a Dexterity Rogue. Unarmored Defense is an AC boost, but the core mechanic is wasted.
You can't deliver Sneak Attack with Eldritch Blast, and low-level Invocations aren't especially useful. If you want spellcasting, Wizard is a much easier choice.

ui.optionalDesc: Effects you can apply by trading Sneak Attack dice.
ui.backgroundNote: Any Background that doesn’t increase Dexterity is immediately out. The Origin Feat from your Background is one of your most important choices.
ui.multiclassNote: Every level outside Rogue delays Sneak Attack scaling, Reliable Talent (level 7), and Slippery Mind (level 15). The bar for a dip is high.
ui.weaponNote: Rogues get 2 Weapon Mastery slots. Focus on Finesse or Light weapons for Sneak Attack eligibility.
ui.armorNote: Rogues are proficient in light armor only.
ui.subclassDesc: Chosen at level 3. 2024 D&D has four subclasses. See the RPGBOT Subclasses Guide for detailed ratings.
ui.featDesc: Origin Feats come from your Background; General Feats fill ASI slots. Dragonmark Feats require an Eberron lineage.
